features.feature: Multiple windows and independent workspace lists
features.acceptance: Create two windows; switching and closing workspaces in one does not mutate the other.
features.implementation: Independent window roots and workspace lists.
features.remaining: Multi-window lifecycle acceptance across platforms.

features.feature: Vertical workspaces and per-pane surface tabs
features.acceptance: Keep window, workspace, pane and surface identities distinct through all operations.
features.implementation: Sidebar workspaces and per-pane terminal tabs. Close Other Tabs provides a policy-aware batch close with stable target identities, keeper preservation and menu/palette/shortcut access. Shared tab rename controls show character limits and preserve overlong drafts for correction; context menus identify captured tab targets. Local post-v0.1.11 fixes tie rename cleanup to terminal close/move lifecycle and preserve drafts on same-tab clicks.
features.remaining: Full identity and interaction parity acceptance.

features.feature: Nested horizontal and vertical splits
features.acceptance: Split recursively, resize dividers, and preserve running sessions.
features.implementation: Nested weighted splits, divider resizing and collapse. Menu/palette/custom actions and explicit-target pane.split RPC support left/right/up/down, inherited directory/font settings and optional focus/activation. Native socket checks verify nested splits, PID continuity and failed-start preservation of zoom/layout.
features.remaining: Cross-platform native interaction and performance gates.

features.feature: Directional and numeric focus navigation
features.acceptance: Keyboard navigation selects the expected pane with no accidental terminal input.
features.implementation: Directional pane focus, numeric workspace shortcuts and Focus Pane 1–9 palette actions with Cmd+Option+number on macOS / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+number elsewhere. Numeric selection follows pane traversal order and moves zoom to the selected pane.
features.remaining: Complete native navigation coverage, including new Select Tab 1–9 shortcuts (Cmd+Shift+number on macOS / Ctrl+Shift+number elsewhere) and palette actions. Missing tab numbers are no-ops; tab numbering is per focused pane.

features.feature: Tab movement, reordering and detaching
features.acceptance: Move a live surface between panes and workspaces without restarting its process.
features.implementation: Tab reorder, movement between panes, palette transfer to named workspaces, tab drops onto sidebar workspaces, and detachment into a new window preserving the terminal entity/PTY with rebound focus subscriptions. Native macOS palette transfer of the last source tab preserved shell PID/state and removed the empty source. Browser pointer reorder uses the native insertion rule; cross-pane drops transfer the existing sample terminal with output/focus preserved and remove empty source panes. Both sole-tab and multi-tab source gestures were checked locally. Transfer resets transient rendering/input state.
features.remaining: Native palette/detachment/sidebar drag and OS-focus acceptance. Live macOS RPC checks now verify the shared cross-window transfer path's PID/state continuity, multi-tab round trip, sole-tab source workspace/window cleanup and stale targets. Busy/restore destinations and complete multi-pane, zoom and cross-platform acceptance remain pending.

features.feature: Workspace movement, reordering and pinning
features.acceptance: Reordering persists and moving a workspace to another window preserves its sessions.
features.implementation: Desktop and browser share workspace drop ordering, group membership moves and pin-tier rejection through rmux-core. Browser reorder and joining/leaving groups were verified with pointer gestures; the detached drag preview uses bundled fonts. Keyboard/drag workspace reorder within pinned/unpinned groups, pin/unpin actions, manual layout persistence of pin state, and movement into new or next existing windows retaining workspace/layout/terminal entities with rebound window subscriptions. Existing-window transfer preserves pinned-group placement and rejects restoring/closing destinations before mutation. A dedicated searchable Move Workspace to Window picker is available in the menu/palette and through a custom shortcut; it captures source identity and destination handles, shows active workspace names/counts and busy state, and reuses the guarded transfer path.
features.remaining: Native acceptance of the dedicated destination picker, movement into new/existing windows, stale destination handling, and pin/reorder/restore behavior across platforms.

features.feature: Workspace names, descriptions, icons and colors
features.acceptance: User labels persist; automatic metadata never silently replaces a manual name.
features.implementation: Manual names/descriptions, preset and custom glyph icons/hex colors, sidebar metadata display, and saved layout persistence with backward-compatible defaults. Browser metadata editing now shares command routing, validation, text editor and preset picker sources; browser UI checks cover save/cancel/clear, invalid inputs, Unicode icons and revealing collapsed targets. Browser metadata is intentionally session-local.
features.remaining: Native acceptance of the new graphical preset icon/color pickers and metadata editing, and visual layout acceptance. Metadata automatic capture and forced-stop restoration have native smoke evidence in docs/benchmarks/session-restore-smoke.md. Preset buttons stage changes in the existing editor with Enter to save and Escape to cancel; custom glyph/hex entry remains supported.

features.feature: Workspace groups and anchor behavior
features.acceptance: Create, collapse, pin, regroup and ungroup; closing the anchor promotes a member without closing siblings.
features.implementation: Window-local ownership and validated layout/session persistence with anchor promotion on close/detach. Sidebar anchor headers, indented/collapsible members, create/rename/pin/ungroup actions, new-group shortcut and header add button. New workspaces join the active group after the active member. Focused model/format tests and desktop compilation pass; native UI acceptance pending.
features.remaining: Sidebar multi-selection acceptance, native acceptance of group cwd overrides and generated-anchor cleanup; native visual/keyboard/drag acceptance. Group create/update/ungroup/add/remove/set-anchor RPC and persistent external identity are implemented and smoke-tested. Ordering, member drag/drop, styling and anchor-position preservation are implemented; native appearance remains unverified.

features.feature: Pane swap, break, join and zoom operations
features.acceptance: Define each operation as a layout transaction with preserved surface identity and focus.
features.implementation: Pane zoom, swap-with-next, geometric left/right/up/down swaps, active-tab break into left/right/above/below split and joins into next or geometric neighbors retain existing terminal entities. A native macOS break-right/swap/join sequence preserved shell PID and variable state.
features.remaining: Complete upstream operation semantics, native directional-swap/join acceptance, multi-tab join order/unread handling, restore interactions and cross-platform acceptance.

features.feature: Command palette and workspace switcher
features.acceptance: Search actions and workspaces; execute the same command path used by shortcuts and CLI.
features.implementation: Action palette, named workspace and terminal switching, numeric pane focus and tab-transfer destinations with ranked per-word fuzzy search and stable entity targeting. Terminal entries include workspace/pane/tab identity and custom titles. Native and WASM provide searchable effective command shortcuts using resolved bindings and shared key-name aliases. Copy, Paste and Previous/Next Pane are now exposed through the shared command catalog and existing action handlers. File previews use literal case-insensitive word filtering in source order, independently of fuzzy command ranking. Shared text fields preserve platform editing combinations and leave unrelated modified keys for parent actions. Preview history/source navigation and context menu/tab chooser polish are implemented; interaction acceptance remains tracked separately.
features.remaining: Full upstream command configuration semantics, accessibility and complete native search/switching acceptance. Configured commands support named shortcuts, literal argv, cwd and child environment overrides; palette launches use background PTY preparation. rmux --command NAME also launches these definitions with the shared PTY command API. A macOS real-PTY smoke check verifies CLI argv/environment/cwd and missing-name failure; cross-platform runtime acceptance remains pending.

features.feature: Close confirmations and active-agent warnings
features.acceptance: Respect configured warnings and distinguish closing a view from terminating owned work.
features.implementation: Tab, workspace and window close requests prompt when any reported task is working or blocked. Window actions and native close callbacks share the warning path; the Quit rmux action scans all windows and confirms once before process cleanup. Confirmation resolves original entity IDs, with tab focus-handle validation; transfers do not ask to terminate processes. Unix foreground process groups and directly launched commands also trigger active-work warnings. The on-demand check uses nonblocking parser/exit-state locks and conservatively requests confirmation under contention; focused real-PTY contention and job-control tests pass.
features.remaining: macOS normal AppKit quit requests now route through confirmation/cleanup; an isolated native probe verifies cancellation/retry/approval. Native confirmation UI acceptance, preserving macOS logout/shutdown requests, other platform-originated quit routing and non-reporting Windows process detection remain pending. Settings now offers persistent Active tasks/Always/Never close confirmation; RMUX_CONFIRM_CLOSE=active|always|never overrides it without changing the saved policy.

features.feature: Focus history and last-prompt navigation
features.acceptance: Return to the previous focus location and last prompt without restoring stale handles.
features.implementation: Last Workspace toggles to a remembered workspace entity per window; reorder preserves the target and closing it clears history. Last Terminal records up to 32 terminal IDs per window and resolves the previous live terminal across panes, tabs and workspaces through menu/palette actions. Previous/Next Prompt use Ghostty semantic viewport navigation through menu, palette and terminal shortcuts. Back/Forward focus actions now keep a separate bounded 64-visit per-window terminal trail, skip closed targets, and branch after a new focus choice. Exposed in menus/palette and custom shortcuts without default bindings. Focused trail tests pass; native integration acceptance remains pending.
features.remaining: Native focus-history and custom-shortcut acceptance, broader shell integration and native prompt-navigation acceptance. Last Terminal/Workspace and prompt navigation are now exposed as configurable shortcut actions. Last Prompt is implemented through menu/palette and jumps to the newest retained semantic prompt, with live-output fallback when no markers exist.

features.feature: Right-side Dock with terminal and browser splits
features.acceptance: Window and workspace Dock layouts restore; focused Dock shortcuts target the Dock.

features.feature: Canvas layout and switching layout mode
features.acceptance: Switch tiled and canvas layouts while preserving surfaces; offscreen panes do not render continuously.

features.feature: Merge one workspace into another
features.acceptance: Move all source surfaces atomically and preserve their order and sessions.
features.implementation: Merge Workspace into menu/palette picker chooses a same-window destination by stable entity ID. Preflight rejects stale/self/busy/depth-limit cases; a synchronous ownership transfer preserves pane/terminal entities and both nested trees, appending the source on the right, reassigning pane ownership/subscriptions and removing the emptied source entry. Destination metadata is retained and zoom clears. Desktop test compilation and split-depth checks pass. rmux workspace.merge RPC and merge-workspace CLI route through the same guarded same-window implementation with explicit distinct IDs and opt-in OS activation; malformed-request queue exclusion and CLI argument tests pass. This is an rmux extension, not a pinned upstream command-name claim. The picker and RPC now resolve destinations across app windows. Cross-window preflight checks both window interaction guards and the destination 256-terminal budget; moved terminals rebind their focus/input subscriptions, and source group/last-window cleanup runs after destination ownership succeeds. Compilation and the RPC routing test pass. The native macOS live-stdio harness also passes same-window and cross-window merges: all seven fixture shells retain PIDs and Unicode variable values, both layout subtrees survive, destination selection and workspace ownership update, stale sources fail without mutation, and the emptied source window closes. All fixture children exit after app termination.
features.remaining: Native live-stdio checks now verify unchanged per-pane tab indices/selections and hidden-tab unread notification records through same-window and cross-window merges. Group/anchor/native-focus/stale-destination behavior, live socket and persistence acceptance remain pending; other platforms and exact upstream semantics remain open.

features.feature: Keyboard click hints
features.acceptance: Hints cover documented UI targets; Escape cancels and terminal keys remain usable.

features.feature: Ghostty terminal state and protocol behavior
features.acceptance: Run shell, editor, alternate-screen, color, mouse and terminal query fixtures on all desktop platforms.
features.implementation: Ghostty state, PTY input/output and incremental terminal rendering.
features.remaining: Full protocol fixtures and native desktop coverage on all platforms.

features.feature: Font fallback, Unicode and text shaping
features.acceptance: Validate CJK, combining marks, emoji and ligatures at multiple DPI values.
features.implementation: GPUI text shaping and cached terminal rows.
features.remaining: CJK, combining marks, emoji, ligature and DPI acceptance matrix.

features.feature: Theme, cursor, background and font settings
features.acceptance: Apply supported settings live; explicitly report unsupported Ghostty settings.
features.implementation: Bounded per-terminal font zoom/reset and configured font family with shared cell metrics, font-sensitive row cache and saved-layout fonts. Live-reloaded hollow/hidden unfocused cursor, default foreground/background/cursor colors and 16-color ANSI palette. Application cursor shapes and OSC color overrides remain honored. Unchanged configured colors/palettes skip engine updates. Built-in Solarized Dark/Light and Nord presets are selectable in Settings and configuration, with explicit color/palette override precedence. Settings previews effective configured text/background/cursor/selection colors and supplied ANSI palettes without creating terminal sessions, with imported-path tooltips. Explicit theme_file loading imports bounded regular UTF-8 files with strict Ghostty-style foreground/background/cursor/cursor-text/selection-background/selection-foreground with engine-parsed X11 names, hex and RGB specifications and sparse ANSI palette assignments with engine-parsed numeric bases, inheriting the selected preset or directly queried pinned engine defaults, with errors for unsupported settings and explicit override precedence. Menu/palette/Settings/custom-action import opens a native picker and parses asynchronously with stale-edit protection; Save persists the path. Imported and explicit selection backgrounds resolve at paint time without reshaping cached rows. Cursor fill supports dynamic cell references while honoring application OSC cursor colors. Imported palettes support indices 0–255 across terminal creation and reload, preserving OSC overrides. Selection backgrounds support dynamic cell references with allocation-free merged paint spans. Selection foregrounds resolve dynamic references per cell, including text decorations and cached run boundaries. Block-cursor text supports literal colors and dynamic cell-foreground/cell-background references through the existing single-glyph cache with effective-color invalidation. Optional selection foreground colors use one lazily cached alternate rendering per selected visible row, clipped separately from normal text; native rendering/performance acceptance pending. Native cursor_opacity supports 0–100% with live Settings adjustment, preview and persistence; block text fades toward its original foreground and zero skips cursor paint. Focused blending, validation, persistence and keyboard-navigation tests pass; native visuals remain pending.
features.remaining: Selection opacity is implemented with Settings/JSON, persistence and focused tests; native visual acceptance remains pending. Seven named presets now include Catppuccin Mocha/Latte with cursor and selection colors and retained upstream licensing. Broader named-theme catalog, native import-picker acceptance and additional Ghostty theme syntax, additional cursor/background settings, native color reload, font/zoom/restore and focus-transition acceptance, and complete configuration acceptance.

features.feature: Opacity, blur, background images and shaders
features.acceptance: Publish per-platform capabilities; enabling effects must pass frame and memory budgets.
features.implementation: Live terminal background opacity (0–100%) and optional platform blur are exposed in Settings and persisted configuration. Only the default terminal fill is translucent; text, explicit colored cell backgrounds and app chrome remain opaque. Parent backgrounds no longer mask transparency, and native background appearance changes only when its mode changes. Focused settings validation/step/save tests and desktop compilation pass.
features.remaining: Native transparency/blur/compositor and performance acceptance across platforms, background images, shaders and full upstream settings semantics.

features.feature: Ghostty keybindings, sequences and key tables
features.acceptance: Document action mapping and precedence; distinguish terminal actions from host actions.
features.implementation: rmux JSON custom bindings support terminal/window action scopes, configured commands, one/two-stroke sequences, prefix validation, precedence and reload. Text targets now send exact bounded UTF-8 input only to the focused terminal, with overlay/prompt guards. Resolved hints and pending chords use platform-style labels without changing GPUI configuration syntax; palette shortcut columns have bounded width. Custom action mapping also exposes menu clipboard, tab/window/quit, layout/session save/open, settings-file/appearance save and diagnostics operations without new handlers or defaults. Focused keymap tests cover text bytes, context exclusion and validation.
features.remaining: Ghostty syntax import, complete action mapping, named key tables and native chord/text input acceptance; this is not a claim of Ghostty configuration compatibility.

features.feature: Selection, clipboard, scrollback and find
features.acceptance: Search and copy from bounded scrollback while output continues; preserve Unicode selections.
features.implementation: Selection, clipboard, bounded scrollback, on-demand find with bounded selection prefill and per-terminal last-query recall, engine-backed Select All, and Clear Scrollback preserving the current screen and restoring history retention. Native pointer gestures, Select All, Clear Scrollback and scrolling now share a bounded interaction queue with nonblocking parser admission. Frames and selection exports flush requests in order, preserving immediate Copy without an intervening frame. Clipboard exports support cooperative cancellation during formatting.
features.remaining: Full Unicode, native interaction and platform acceptance.

features.feature: Bracketed paste and large input delivery
features.acceptance: Deliver large and multiline input in order without interleaving control bytes or losing input.
features.implementation: Bounded input queue; up to 1 MiB UTF-8 paste in one writer message, with one queued/in-flight paste per session. Focused limit/permit tests and macOS PTY delivery of 140 KB Unicode/multiline text followed by ordinary input passed.
features.allocation_progress: Native paste reserves the bounded writer queue without parser-lock admission; the writer resolves bracketed-paste mode and checks cancellation while waiting. Borrowed payloads allocate after obtaining the one-paste permit; owned strings move into the queue. Automation retains its opportunistic admission contract. Ten paste-focused tests pass, including cancellation and concurrent output delivery without native admission retries.
features.remaining: Native clipboard/cancellation and delivery acceptance across platforms, sustained saturation and UI latency measurements. A focused macOS real-PTY test passes exact 896 KiB Unicode bracketed-paste delivery followed by ordered input with a concurrent output producer exceeding 250 KB; no writer error or retained paste permit.

features.feature: Shell integration and working-directory tracking
features.acceptance: Follow directory changes and prompt boundaries across supported shells; avoid per-pane git polling.
features.implementation: OSC 7 directory tracking, sidebar labels, new-shell directory inheritance, and automatically loaded zsh hooks emitting OSC 133 boundaries plus encoded directory reports. Private temporary wrappers preserve user startup order and ZDOTDIR; environment opt-out is supported. Fish automatically loads after user configuration via --init-command in both login modes. Bash 4.4+ command-start markers use PS0 while preserving user content and avoiding DEBUG traps; Bash 3.2 compatibility and Linux Bash 5.2.21 PS0 emission/preservation fixtures pass, with path-filtered GitHub CI. Attribute-aware plain/exported PROMPT_COMMAND arrays preserve hook order and captured exit status; Bash 5.2.21 execution and Bash 3.2 structural compatibility checks pass. Automatically loaded PowerShell script wraps the original prompt with OSC 7 and OSC 133 A/B; mise-managed PowerShell 7.5.4 runtime checks pass for prompt text/status, Unicode URI escaping, duplicate sourcing and provider filtering. Private startup script loads after normal profiles without changing execution policy; macOS real-PTY profile, Unicode-directory and prompt-navigation fixture passes. Existing console reader is delegated to for nonempty-command OSC 133 C and next-prompt D without a guessed exit code; empty/canceled reads emit no command markers. Runtime fixtures and macOS PTY reader activation pass. Native PSReadLine/theme and Windows acceptance remain pending.
features.remaining: Automatic Bash login loading, older fish fallback acceptance, PowerShell exact native completion exit codes and native interactive acceptance (normalized success/failure is implemented and focused-tested), broader prompt-theme/global-startup compatibility, Linux runtime validation and native acceptance. Non-login Bash auto-loads via RMUX_SHELL_LOGIN=0; manual Bash and fish scripts are present. Fish 4.9.3 startup checks pass on macOS and Ubuntu CI, and native macOS PTY checks pass; native fish markers are used to avoid duplicate integration hooks.

features.feature: Git branch, PR and listening-port metadata
features.acceptance: Update the correct workspace asynchronously with bounded polling and explicit unknown states.
features.implementation: Sidebar branch/detached-HEAD context reads bounded Git metadata in background on directory reports, with worktree indirection and coalesced requests. On-demand local TCP listener panel scans shell descendants off the UI thread with one global scan permit and 128 retained rows. A macOS loopback ownership test and ARM64 Linux compilation pass; native UI, process churn and remote/automatic port metadata remain incomplete. Listening Ports offers an explicit Open as HTTP button and O shortcut through the default browser, mapping wildcard listeners to loopback while keeping scoped IPv6 copy-only; URL mapping tests pass, native browser activation remains unverified. Manual PR refresh uses authenticated GitHub CLI with a ten-second timeout, global single-flight limit, 64-KiB response limit and local branch validation before/after lookup. Sidebar context shows PR number/state/title or explicit no-result/unavailable status; palette/custom shortcut can open its HTTPS URL. Cwd/branch changes clear cached PR data. PR lookup prefers a unique open PR, then falls back to a unique result across all states; multiple matches have an explicit ambiguity status and no clickable arbitrary result. Both queries share the ten-second budget. PR context has a separate sidebar line; branch/directory retain their original layout. Completed local port scans retain a compact sidebar snapshot with four unique port numbers, overflow count and partial-result marking; it follows the selected terminal and is hidden after process exit.
features.remaining: Native PR lookup/open-link/sidebar visual acceptance, enterprise/fork repository selection and cross-platform runtime coverage; native port-snapshot lifecycle/visual acceptance, automatic metadata refresh policy and full metadata parity. PR lookup and port snapshots remain explicit, not recurring polling.

features.feature: Clickable URLs and local or remote file paths
features.acceptance: Route URLs and paths correctly; remote paths never open an unrelated same-named local file.
features.implementation: Modifier-click opens OSC 8 and plain-text HTTP(S) links through the platform browser. On-demand detection supports wide Unicode cells and fully visible soft-wrapped logical lines up to 8 KiB; clipped plain URLs are rejected. Explicit OSC 8 targets take precedence. Modifier-hover now shows target tooltips and an eligible-link pointer cursor, caching per displayed cell/revision and skipping parser contention. Click and hover share URL allow rules; pointer exit/modifier release/click/window transfer/frame changes clear stale targets. Dedicated hover previews are bounded to the window with ellipsized target text. The terminal context menu captures the opening-position link for Copy Link Address/Open Link, preserving the chosen target through output changes and routing eligible HTTP(S) and local file targets. Desktop compilation passed. Local file:// OSC 8 and plain-text links now resolve through the configured external-editor path, shared by modifier-click, context-menu activation and hover eligibility. Resolution is bounded and performs no filesystem access on hover. Remote URL hosts, recognized remote terminal contexts, network-share forms, query/fragment targets and control characters are rejected. Routing and terminal hyperlink tests pass, including decoded Unicode/literal shell metacharacters and displayed-frame lookup. Plain path-shaped tokens and extension-bearing line references now route absolute or terminal-cwd-relative files, including line/column suffixes, through literal editor argv placeholders. Unicode/soft-wrap lookup, remote rejection, bounded coordinates and placeholder preservation have focused tests. Quoted path detection preserves spaces and punctuation; local ~/ paths now resolve against the home directory with line/column support, without shell evaluation or filesystem access.
features.remaining: Native modifier-click/menu-to-editor acceptance, Windows/Linux runtime coverage, native acceptance of quoted paths and home-directory expansion, historical output cwd association, and remote file routing. Remote inference cannot identify every manually launched SSH session; recognized remote contexts never route file links to the local editor. Browser demo local-editor launching is intentionally unavailable.

features.feature: Image paste, file drop and remote upload
features.acceptance: Transfer to the correct host, quote resulting paths, and clean bounded temporary storage.
features.implementation: macOS/Linux external file drops into a focused terminal paste POSIX-quoted absolute paths through the bounded bracketed-paste queue without reading contents or adding Enter. Focus/overlay/quit guards, 256-path and 64 KiB limits, UTF-8/control validation and a real POSIX shell quoting fixture are implemented. Image-only clipboard paste writes original bytes on a background executor to private temporary files, then queues a quoted path after focus/overlay revalidation. Per-image 16 MiB and app-wide 32-file/64 MiB reservations bound live storage; terminal lifetime owns cleanup. Storage/permissions/quota tests pass. New images use a private user-cache directory with a nonblocking publication lock and per-file lifetime locks. Each background paste sweeps at most 512 entries, removing only unlocked rmux image files; focused lock/orphan/unrelated-file/symlink checks pass. macOS Finder copied-file paste reads per-item file URLs through AppKit, bounds paths/counts, rejects remote hosts and changed clipboard snapshots, and shares the quoted-path queue. Native NSURL decoding tests pass without touching the system clipboard; Finder end-to-end acceptance remains pending.
features.remaining: Native Finder/file-manager drag and clipboard-image acceptance, forced-termination/cross-process recovery acceptance, Windows shell quoting, remote upload/routing and full platform/protocol acceptance.

features.feature: Program status over OSC 7501
features.acceptance: Handle status priority, prompt reset and focus acknowledgement without conflating agent lifecycle.
features.implementation: Bounded OSC 7501 records with lifecycle cleanup, tab summaries/attention and an on-demand full-record detail view with hierarchy and inherited app names.
features.remaining: Full reply-content acceptance, native detail-view accessibility/layout, lifecycle ordering and complete protocol acceptance.

features.feature: Terminal screenshots, screen reads and selection reads
features.acceptance: Capture the addressed surface without stealing focus; bound response size and scrollback reads.
features.implementation: Bounded viewport/history RPC reads and background selection export. UTF-8-safe streaming selection/history tests pass without selection or viewport changes.
features.remaining: Native selected-text RPC acceptance and graphical surface screenshot capture.

features.feature: Terminal copy mode and buffers
features.acceptance: Validate copy-mode and buffer semantics separately from ordinary clipboard operations.
features.implementation: Bounded asynchronous history snapshot with virtualized copy-mode rows, keyboard and mouse line-range selection, Unicode clipboard copy and Select All. Snapshot text stays stable while output continues. Submitted literal searches share the snapshot, run off the UI thread and navigate matching lines with wraparound. Keyboard character ranges preserve Unicode graphemes and highlight selected spans, with bounded long-line display following the cursor. Vertical movement retains Unicode terminal-cell columns using sparse checkpoints built off the UI thread. Rectangular keyboard selections use cell columns, preserve whole edge graphemes and format cancellably in the background. Process-local bounded named buffers support set/list CLI commands and set/list/get/delete RPC with explicit quotas and no persistence. paste-buffer CLI and buffer.paste RPC target explicit surfaces through the existing bounded input path, without consuming buffers or changing focus/viewport. Copy-mode Save Buffer formats selections in the background, enforces quotas and rejects stale saves using store revisions. A searchable named-buffer paste picker captures its originating surface and rejects changed buffer revisions before queueing. A named-buffer delete picker releases storage and rejects stale revisions. set-buffer accepts omitted text or dash as bounded UTF-8 stdin without newline trimming. The pinned CLI contract describes upstream copy-mode as a placeholder; rmux copy-mode UI is additional functionality.
features.remaining: Native input/layout acceptance, remaining upstream CLI/RPC semantics.

features.feature: Window video recording and terminal output piping
features.acceptance: Capture own-window/region MP4 and GIF with start/stop/status/list, captions, duration limits and atomic final output replacement; separately pipe selected surface text with bounded queues and child cleanup.
features.remaining: Window capture/encoder backends, recording lifecycle/captions, local-only routing and atomic clip publication; pipe-pane implicit selectors, Windows execution and broader process/runtime acceptance.
features.implementation: pipe-pane captures a bounded history snapshot via RPC, optionally limited to the last 1–65536 logical lines with --lines or selected text with --selection and optional --preserve-wraps, then feeds a local CLI shell command; output is inherited and exit status propagated by default. --json captures stdout/stderr with a 1 MiB retention cap per stream, truncation flags and exit status; concurrent readers drain while input is written. Truncated captures reject before execution. Focused CLI/process tests passed.

features.feature: Predictive local echo for remote sessions
features.acceptance: Correct predictions when remote echo differs; never predict password input or corrupt TUIs.

features.feature: Password indicator and optional editing gestures
features.acceptance: Track echo state accurately and limit prompt-editing gestures to eligible shell contexts.
features.implementation: Event-driven local macOS/Linux PTY echo/canonical sampling with an Input hidden badge for focused canonical no-echo input. Real PTY transition fixture passed; raw-mode TUIs excluded.
features.remaining: Native badge/input acceptance, silent-mode transition freshness, remote/ConPTY password detection and optional eligible-prompt editing gestures.

features.feature: Remote OSC 52 clipboard permission
features.acceptance: Scope clipboard consent to the remote source and permit revocation.

features.feature: Hard-wrap copy reflow and per-session shell history
features.acceptance: Preserve user-selected copy policy and restore session history without duplicating prompt execution.
features.implementation: Copy modes and bounded streaming exports are implemented. Experimental opt-in per-terminal Bash/zsh history now connects private bounded storage, independent restore identities, event-driven background saves, native history import, session references, visible errors, and reader-drain-aware quit flushing. An isolated real-shell save/restore roundtrip passes with global history emptied before restore.
features.remaining: Retention cleanup, individual history-entry deletion synchronization, broader shell support, native GUI lifecycle acceptance, and broader reflow acceptance remain pending. History is off by default; shell_history_directory enables the supported local-shell path.

features.feature: Hidden terminal renderer reclamation
features.acceptance: Release inactive GPU surfaces without killing shells or losing terminal state; recreate correctly on focus.
features.implementation: Inactive tabs are unmounted while sessions remain retained. Row and cursor caches are explicitly released for hidden panes/tabs. Desktop-owned cell snapshots are replaced with shared empty-row placeholders preserving dimensions, with a fresh engine frame fetched on next prepaint; engine state is retained. Selection-specific shaped glyph and decoration variants are also dropped when their row is deselected or the foreground setting changes; active variants remain cached. Focused row-cache ownership regressions pass.
features.remaining: Native refocus/engine-busy placeholder acceptance, demonstrated renderer resource reclamation and memory budgets.

features.feature: OSC 9, 99 and 777 notifications
features.acceptance: Route notification sequences to their originating surface and deduplicate hook overlap.
features.implementation: OSC 9/777 callback with bounded latest-message storage and unread markers for unfocused terminals; focused protocol test passed.
features.remaining: Full OSC 99 lifecycle/action semantics and native acceptance. Bounded 32-message history and burst delivery are implemented. Bounded chunked title/body, streaming Base64/Unicode assembly, capability queries and always/unfocused/invisible filtering are implemented.

features.feature: Pane rings, unread badges and notification panel
features.acceptance: Read, dismiss, clear and jump actions keep pane and workspace unread state consistent.
features.implementation: BEL/OSC unread markers and pane borders, next-unread navigation, and a newest-first 32-message-per-terminal panel with copy, expansion, per-message acknowledgement and dismissal. Fresh macOS live socket smoke verifies CLI acknowledgement retains history, preserves another unread message, is idempotent and leaves workspace selection unchanged.
features.remaining: Complete notification lifecycle semantics, native panel accessibility and interaction/appearance acceptance. Per-terminal 32-message history, message-specific read/dismiss state and stable keyboard targets are implemented.

features.feature: Native desktop notifications and focus suppression
features.acceptance: Implement OS adapters; respect focused-surface and app-wide suppression settings.
features.implementation: Opt-in native_notifications setting and Settings toggle; lazy single dispatcher with eight queued weak terminal references, one delivery per second, configurable unfocused-terminal/background-app policy and read/dismissed/closed suppression before dispatch, bounded plain-text payloads, and asynchronous error reporting. notify-rust uses modern macOS Notification Center, XDG and Windows backends; Windows uses rmux AppUserModelID and still needs installer registration. macOS/Linux click routing resolves current terminal ownership with up to 16 async response listeners and two-minute expiry; XDG close requests have a separate two-second bound; the vendored adapter fixes canceled-response registration cleanup. ARM64 Linux and macOS compilation pass; native permission/delivery/click behavior, Windows click routing and multi-window focus/platform acceptance remain incomplete.

features.feature: Cloud workspaces, terminal control and layouts
features.acceptance: Keep remote processes and layout authoritative beyond desktop disconnection.

features.feature: Cloud files, environment and project setup

features.feature: Cloud networking, domains, ports and VPN

features.feature: Cloud desktop displays and computer use

features.feature: Cloud base machine, snapshots and forks
